sammendrag: Dropout rates in Spain decreased from 70% in 1977 to 30% at the end of the 90s, but remained at roughly 30% ever since. Dropout rates are defined as the % of the population aged 18‐24 with at most lower secondary degree (corresponding to 16 years old if there are no repetitions) and not in further education or training. This paper analyses the role of the educational law (LOGSE) from 1990, and other factors, in explaining why school dropout stopped its declining trend in the last two decades. Differences in the timing of implementation of the LOGSE across different regions are used to identify whether this law contributed in deterring the rate of improvement of the dropout rates observed in years before. Results show a negative relationship between the LOGSE and the incidence of school dropout. We also find significant differences in the behavior of male and female students.
tittel: WHY SCHOOL DROPOUT REMAINED SO HIGH IN SPAIN IN THE LAST TWO DECADES? THE ROLE OF THE EDUCATIONAL LAW (LOGSE)
